prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t pick a single “best” roofer for Denver without knowing your exact location and priorities, and I don’t have live local search. What I can do is:

- Help you find the highest-rated local roofing contractors if you give your ZIP code or neighborhood.  
- Give a short, practical checklist and the right questions to ask so you can identify the best contractor for hail-damage repair.

If you want me to look up local options, tell me your ZIP code. Otherwise, use the checklist below when evaluating roofers for hail damage:

Checklist — how to choose the best Denver roofer for hail damage
1. License, insurance, and permits
   - Ask for proof of general liability insurance and workers’ comp. Call the carrier to verify.
   - Confirm the contractor pulls required city/county permits.

2. Storm-damage and insurance experience
   - Choose a roofer experienced with insurance claims and Xactimate estimates.
   - Ask if they will meet the insurance adjuster on-site, document damage, and provide supplemental claims if needed.

3. Certifications and workmanship warranty
   - Look for manufacturer certifications (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning, etc.).
   - Get written warranties for both materials (manufacturer) and workmanship (contractor).

4. Estimates and contracts
   - Get at least 2–3 written, itemized estimates (scope, materials, removal, disposal, timelines).
   - Contract should include start/end dates, payment schedule, cleanup, and a lien waiver upon final payment.

5. References and reputation
   - Check recent Google/Yelp reviews, BBB rating, and ask for local references from jobs done within the last year.
   - Look for example photos of completed hail repair jobs in Denver’s climate.

6. Red flags / things to avoid
   - Door-to-door storm chasers pressuring you to sign immediately.
   - Requiring full payment up front or only accepting cash.
   - No physical business address, no contract, or poor communication.

7. Pricing and scope
   - Be wary of unusually low bids — they often skip permit fees, proper underlayment, or use inferior shingles.
   - Confirm whether the scope includes replacing damaged decking, flashing, vents, and gutters if needed.

8. Final paperwork
   - Get a final lien release and copies of permits and inspection sign-offs.
   - Make sure the contractor coordinates any insurance check/payment and provides all receipts.

Typical process for hail damage
1. Document damage (photos/video, date, post-storm).  
2. Call your insurance agent to report the claim.  
3. Get 2–3 written estimates from reputable roofers.  
4. Meet adjuster with your chosen contractor; contractor documents loss and submits estimate.  
5. Contractor obtains permits, completes work, and provides paperwork for the insurance company.

If you share your ZIP code or neighborhood, I’ll suggest several well-reviewed Denver roofers you can contact and provide a short script of questions to use when calling them.
